[CRITICAL] OWASP A07: The authentication mechanism for the Antigravity Link HTTP API is not defined. The Client Intel report explicitly flagged the port/authentication requirement as a research gap. In Section 4.2 of `03_architecture.md`, the HTTP POST payload to `http://localhost:11434/v1/devio/invoke` lacks an authentication header. If the API is unauthenticated, this is a severe security risk allowing unauthorized local processes to trigger agents. If it requires authentication, the current design will fail. Please define the authentication mechanism, update the payload schema to include the required headers, and specify how the extension host will securely retrieve this credential.

Good catch on the OWASP A07 risk. I have updated `03_architecture.md` (Sections 4.2 and 6) to define the authentication mechanism. The Extension Host will securely retrieve the user's Antigravity API key using the IDE's native `SecretStorage` API (`context.secrets`) and pass it as a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header of the HTTP POST request. This guarantees the key is never stored in plaintext on disk. Please review the updated architecture.

The defined authentication mechanism using `SecretStorage` and the `Authorization: Bearer` header fully mitigates the OWASP A07 security risk. All architectural and security concerns have been successfully addressed. Architecture approved.

(2) SecretStorage: bearer token stored via VS Code SecretStorage API — verify no token is ever logged or included in IPC messages to the webview. Top 3 implementation constraints for the Developer: (1) NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 must be scoped to the AgLinkClient HTTPS agent only — use the https module agent option or a per-request override. NEVER set process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED globally. (2) All 5 settings (devio.autonomyMode, devio.antigravityLinkPort, devio.freshConversationPerTurn, devio.newChatSelector, devio.responseSelector) MUST be declared in package.json contributes.configuration before any code reads them. Hard-coding any default value in TypeScript instead of reading it from the VS Code config is a QA defect. (3) ConversationManager.openFreshChat() timeout is hard-capped at 10 000ms. Do not expose this as a configurable setting. The method must catch its own TimeoutError and emit a WARN to the webview — it must NOT propagate the error to OrchestrationEngine (which would halt the loop). Degraded isolation (continuing in existing conversation) is acceptable; a halted engine is not.

QA-ARCH-001 [HIGH] — §3.1 / §4.1: TLS bypass mechanism is insufficiently specified. The spec states NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 must be scoped to the AgLinkClient instance, but Node.js built-in fetch (undici) does not support per-request TLS override via a simple agent option like the https module. The architecture must specify the exact mechanism: use undici.Agent({connect: {rejectUnauthorized: false}}) as the dispatcher option passed to fetch, instantiated inside AgLinkClient and never exposed globally. Without this specificity, the Developer is at high risk of applying process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = "0" globally, which disables TLS verification process-wide for the entire VS Code extension host — a security boundary violation.
